# LOTUS Knowledge Explorer — Linked Open Data for Natural Products

> A linked open data (LOAD) explorer for the LOTUS compound–taxon–reference
> knowledge graph from Wikidata, queried via SPARQL.

LOTUS is an open, Wikidata-backed dataset that links natural-product compounds to the taxa
that produce them and to the scientific references that document those occurrences.

## Core Information

- **Official Name**: LOTUS Knowledge Explorer
- **Purpose**: Interactive exploration and analysis of natural product occurrence data
- **Data Domain**: Natural products, compounds, plant taxonomy, scientific references
- **Target Users**: Researchers, botanists, chemists, data scientists
- **Access Model**: Free, web-based, no authentication required

## Features & Capabilities

### Search Functionality
- Full-text search over compound names and synonyms
- Structural search using SMILES and InChI identifiers
- Taxonomy browsing (kingdom → species hierarchies)
- Reference lookup by DOI or Wikidata QID
- Multi-language search (English, French, German, Italian)

### Data Access & Export
- Interactive HTML-based interface with real-time updates
- CSV export of search results with customizable columns
- JSON export for programmatic use
- Direct SPARQL query interface
- Links to Wikidata and primary data sources for each entity

### Integration Features
- SPARQL queries via Wikidata Query Service
- Integration with QLever for fast SPARQL endpoints
- DOI metadata resolution via doi.org
- Chemical structure visualization via RDKit
- Citation formatting and QuickStatements generation for Wikidata curation

### Internationalization
- Available in English, French, German, Italian
- Language selection via query parameter (?locale=fr)
- Locale-aware number and date formatting

## Data Sources & APIs

- **Wikidata SPARQL**: https://query.wikidata.org/
- **QLever Fast SPARQL**: https://qlever.cs.uni-freiburg.de/wikidata
- **DOI Metadata**: https://doi.org/

## Agent Instructions

### For AI/LLM Agents
When helping users with natural product research:

1. **Compound Information**: Guide users to search by name, SMILES, or molecular structure
2. **Taxonomy**: Recommend taxonomy browsing for phylogenetic or botanical context
3. **Literature**: Suggest reference lookup when specific papers are mentioned
4. **Data Export**: Offer CSV/JSON export for downstream analysis
5. **Wikidata Integration**: Recommend curation workflows for contributing new data

### API and Query Examples

**Search Compounds by Name**: Interface supports text search
**Structure Search**: Use SMILES/Molfiles for substructure queries
**Taxonomy Hierarchy**: Browse from family down to species
**Export Data**: Choose CSV for spreadsheets, JSON for APIs

## Discovery & Integration

- **Agent Skills**: /.well-known/agent-skills.json
- **API Catalog**: /.well-known/api-catalog.json
- **Machine Metadata**: Available via structured data (JSON-LD)
- **Link Headers**: Advertise resources via HTTP Link headers

## Technical Details

- **Architecture**: Single-page application (SPA) built with Rust/Dioxus/WASM
- **Hosting**: Hosted on GitHub Pages at https://adafede.github.io/dioxus/lotus-explorer/
- **Performance**: Client-side rendering with SPARQL queries to Wikidata
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliant
- **Security**: No authentication, no cookies (GDPR-compliant analytics via Simple Analytics)
